questions.question: Name a unit designed for wet and dry bulb thermometers to protect temperature sensors from being affected by direct or reflected sunlight.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stevenson screen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A Stevenson screen **serves as a protective shelter for meteorological instruments, such as **wet and dry bulb thermometers,** safeguarding them from direct sunlight and precipitation while facilitating free airflow.
 
• These screens are typically constructed from wood and painted white to reflect solar radiation effectively.
 
• Featuring louvered sides, Stevenson screens enable unrestricted air circulation around the thermometers, ensuring accurate temperature measurements.
 
• Moreover, they are strategically positioned 1.25 meters above the ground to minimize the influence of strong temperature gradients present at ground level.
 
• Thomas Stevenson, a notable Scottish civil engineer, credited with the design of the Stevenson screen in 1864. He is also recognized as the father of the renowned writer Robert Louis Stevenson.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thomas Stevenson **was a pioneering Scottish civil engineer, renowned for his contributions to lighthouse design and meteorology. He designed over thirty lighthouses in and around Scotland, as well as the Stevenson screen used in meteorology.
 
• His innovative designs revolutionized lighthouse construction and set a new standard in the field.
 
• Stevenson held prestigious positions throughout his career, including serving as president of the Royal Scottish Society of Arts from 1859 to 1860 and as president of the Royal Society of Edinburgh from 1884 to 1886.
 
• Additionally, he played a key role as a co-founder of the Scottish Meteorological Society.

questions.question: The inertia of an object is measured by its ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Mass.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mass is a measure of inertia of the object, for an object, its inertia would depend on its mass.**
 
• Inertia is the property of an object by virtue of which it opposes any event that attempts to put the object in motion or to change its velocity.
 
• Therefore, an object at rest would want to continue staying at rest and an object in motion would have a tendency to continue its motion.
 
• Greater the mass of the object will be the tendency to resist the events.
 
• Hence,** mass is a measure of the inertia of the object.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's first law of motion** states that "An object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion with the same speed and in the same direction unless acted upon by an unbalanced force." Objects tend to "keep on doing what they're doing." In fact, it is the natural tendency of objects to resist changes in their state of motion. This tendency to resist changes in their state of motion is described as** inertia.**
 
• **Inertia**:
 
 
• The resistance an object has to a change in its state of motion.
 
• All objects resist changes in their state of motion. All objects have this tendency - they have inertia.
 
 
 
• **Volume:** Volume is a scalar quantity expressing the amount of three-dimensional space enclosed by a closed surface.
 
• **Speed: **It is defined as the ratio of distance over time.

questions.question: ______ states that the rates of diffusion of gases are inversely proportional to the square roots of their densities under similar conditions of temperature and pressure.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Graham's Law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Graham's law** states that the rates of **diffusion of gases are inversely proportional to the square roots of their molar masses under similar conditions of temperature and pressure.**
 
• This means that a gas with a lower molar mass will diffuse more quickly than a gas with a higher molar mass.
 
• **For example, hydrogen (H2) has a molar mass of 2.016 g/mol, while oxygen (O2) has a molar mass of 32.000 g/mol.**
 
• This means that hydrogen will diffuse **4.5 times faster than oxygen at the same temperature and pressure.**
 
• Graham's law can be used to calculate the rate of diffusion of a gas.
 
• **The formula for Graham's law is: r = k * √(M)**
 
• **Where**:
 
 
• **r **is the rate of **diffusion**
 
• **k **is a **constant**
 
• **M** is the** molar mass of the gas**
 
 
 
• **The value of k can be determined experimentally.**
 
• **Graham's law** is a useful tool for understanding the behaviour of gases.
 
• **It can be used to predict how gases will diffuse, and it can be used to calculate the rate of diffusion of a gas.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Tyndall's Law** states that the scattering of a beam of light by particles in a** medium is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the wavelength of ligh**t.

 
 
• This means that shorter wavelengths of** light are scattered more easily than longer wavelengths.**
 
 
 
• **Pascal's Law** states that pressure exerted anywhere in an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally in all directions throughout the fluid.
 
 
• This means that if you increase the** pressure at one point in a fluid, the pressure will increase at all points in the fluid.**
 
 
 
• **Kepler's Laws** are three laws that describe the motion of planets around the sun.
 
 
• The first law states that planets orbit the sun in elliptical orbits.
 
• The second law states that the speed of a planet is **greatest when it is closest to the sun and least when it is farthest from the sun.**
 
• The third law states that the square of the** period of a planet's orbit is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit.**

questions.question: When milk is converted into curd, which type of change is it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chemical Change.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chemical change:-**

 
 
• This type of change alters the composition of the substance and results in the formation of a new substance. Examples include combustion, rusting, and digestion. When milk is converted into curd, it undergoes a chemical change.
 
• This change is irreversible, meaning it cannot be undone.
 
• The process of converting milk into curd is called fermentation, which is a chemical reaction that occurs due to the presence of bacteria.
 
• During fermentation, the lactose in the milk is converted into lactic acid, which causes the milk to thicken and form curd.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reversible change: **

 
 
• This type of change can be undone, meaning the original substance can be restored. Examples include melting and freezing of ice.
 
 
 
• **Physical change: **
 
 
• This type of change does not alter the composition of the substance. Examples include changes in state (solid, liquid, gas) and changes in shape or size.
 
 
 
• **Isothermal change: **
 
 
• This type of change occurs at a constant temperature and does not involve any change in energy.

questions.question: The total pressure of a mixture of ideal gases is the sum of partial pressures. This is ______ law of partial pressures.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This is known as Dalton's law of partial pressures.
 
• According to Dalton's law, the total pressure exerted by a mixture of non-reacting ideal gases is equal to the sum of the partial pressures of each individual gas.
 
• Dalton's law is based on the assumption that the gases in the mixture behave independently of one another, without any significant interactions or reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Boyle's Law:**

 
 
• Boyle's law states that, at a constant temperature, the volume of a given amount of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure.
 
• In other words,** as the pressure of a gas increases, its volume decreases, and vice versa, provided the temperature remains constant.** Mathematically, Boyle's law can be expressed as:
 
• **P₁V₁ = P₂V₂**
 
• where** P₁ and V₁ **are the** initial pressure** and **volume**, and **P₂ and V₂** are the **final pressure and volume**, respectively.
 
 
 
• **Charles's Law:**
 
 
• **Charles's law** states that, at a constant pressure, the volume of a given amount of gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature. This means that as the temperature of a gas increases, its volume also increases, and as the temperature decreases, its volume decreases, as long as the pressure remains constant. Mathematically, Charles's law can be expressed as:
 
• **V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂**
 
• where **V₁ and T₁ **are the initial **volume and temperature (in Kelvin), **and** V₂ and T₂ **are the **final volume and temperature**, respectively.
 
 
 
• **Avogadro's Law:**
 
 
• **Avogadro's law states** that, at a constant temperature and pressure, equal volumes of gases contain an equal number of particles (atoms, molecules, or ions).
 
• This law implies that the volume of a gas is directly proportional to the number of moles of gas present. Mathematically, Avogadro's law can be expressed as:
 
• **V₁/n₁ = V₂/n₂**
 
 

where** V₁ and n₁ **are the** initial volume** and number of** moles**, and **V₂ and n₂** are the **final volume **and number of **moles,** respectively.

questions.question: Name the transuranium element with atomic number 106, created by bombarding californium⁻²⁴⁹ with oxygen⁻¹⁸ nuclei.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seaborgium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Seaborgium,** with the **atomic number 106,** is classified as a transuranium element. It is artificially created by** bombarding californium⁻²⁴⁹ with oxygen⁻¹⁸ nuclei**.
 
• As a synthetic element, seaborgium is solid at room temperature and belongs to the transition metal group. Its most stable isotope, seaborgium⁻²⁶⁶, has a half-life of 27.3 seconds.
 
• In 1994, the proposal to name element 106 "seaborgium" was made in tribute to Glenn T. Seaborg, the scientist credited with discovering the transuranium elements.
 
• Seaborg, an American chemist, was awarded the 1951 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for his pioneering work in the field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dubnium (Db)** is an artificially generated radioactive transuranium element situated in Group Vb of the periodic table, with an atomic number of 105. The discovery of dubnium, much like that of rutherfordium (element 104), has been the subject of contention between Soviet and American scientists.
 
• **Hassium (Hs)** is another artificially produced element belonging to the transuranium group, with an atomic number of 108. It was first synthesized and identified in 1984 by researchers from West Germany at the Institute for Heavy Ion Research (Gesellschaft für Schwerionenforschung [GSI]) in Darmstadt.
 
• **Copernicium** is a synthetic chemical element characterized by the symbol Cn and atomic number 112. Its known isotopes are profoundly radioactive and have exclusively been generated within laboratory settings.

questions.question: Aqua regia is an acidic, corrosive and oxidative mixture consisting of ________ volume/volumes of concentrated hydrochloric acid and one volume of concentrated nitric acid, often used to dissolve gold and platinum.

__
 
• Aqua Regia (Latin for “royal water”) is an acidic, corrosive, and oxidative mixture of **three parts** concentrated hydrochloric acid (HCl) and one part concentrated nitric acid (HNO3).
 
• Aqua regia or nitro-hydrochloric acid is a highly corrosive mixture of acids, a fuming yellow or red solution. 
 
• Aqua regia or nitro-hydrochloric acid is a highly corrosive mixture of acids, a fuming yellow or red solution.

questions.question: In cell biology, what is a large double-membraned organelle that is sometimes referred to as the ‘central unit’ of the cell because it contains the chromosomes that bear genetic material?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Nucleus.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The nucleus **is a large double-membraned organelle that is sometimes referred to as the ‘central unit’ of the cell because it contains the chromosomes that bear genetic material.

 
 
• It is a** membrane-bound organelle** found in **eukaryotic cells**.
 
• The main structures making up the nucleus are the **nuclear envelope, a double membrane that encloses the entire organelle and isolates its contents from the cellular cytoplasm.** 
 
• The** nuclear matrix **(which includes the nuclear lamina), is a** network within the nucleus that adds mechanical support, much like the cytoskeleton supports the cell as a whole.**
 
• It contains** DNA arranged in chromosomes.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Peroxisome**

 
 
• Peroxisomes are** small, membrane-enclosed organelles** that contain enzymes involved in a variety of metabolic reactions, including several aspects of **energy metabolism.**
 
 
 
• **Mitochondrion**
 
 
• Mitochondria are **membrane-bound cell organelles **that generate most of the chemical energy needed to power the cell's biochemical reactions.
 
• Chemical energy produced by the mitochondria is stored in a small molecule called **adenosine triphosphate (ATP).**
 
 
 
• **Lysosome**
 
 
• **Membrane-enclosed organelles **contain an** array of enzymes **capable of breaking down all types of** biological polymers—proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates, and lipids.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The LED (light-emitting diode) **is a** PN junction device **that emits light when a current passes through it in the forward direction, i.e. when LED is forward biased, it emits light.
 
• In an LED, this energy lies in the visible region of electromagnetic radiation, and the photon released is perceived as light.
 
• An LED in this way converts electrical energy into light energy.
 
• In reverse biased mode, it works like a normal diode and does not emit light.
 
• It is an optical semiconductor device that emits light when voltage is applied means it converts electrical energy into light energy.
 
• **When Light Emitting Diode (LED) is forward biased, the free electrons from the n-side and the holes from the p-side are pushed towards the junction.**
 
• Light-emitting diodes emit either visible light or invisible infrared light when forward biased.
 
• The LEDs which emit invisible infrared light are used for remote controls.
 
• **LEDs that can emit red, yellow, orange, green, and blue light are available for commercial use.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: ______ is the tube that carries urine from the kidney to the urinary bladder.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ureter.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In humans, the kidney is one of the main organs of the excretory system.
 
• The kidney's function is the filtration of the blood and removing waste(toxic) products.
 
• Waste products and excess fluid are removed through the urine.
 
• If the kidney fails person needs to undergo dialysis.
 
• Dialysis is a treatment that filters and purifies the blood using a machine
 
• The human excretory system includes certain organs that eliminate the wastes such as salts, carbon dioxide, urea, uric acid and water produced by the body.
 
• The path of the urine in the human excretory system is -
 
• After filtering from the kidney → The urine through Ureter → Stored in the Urinary bladder → Exits through the urethra.

questions.question: Which of the following is **not **a good conductor of electricity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diamond.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Among the options, only diamond is NOT a good conductor of electricity**__.
 
• **Diamond** is a naturally-occurring solid.
 __
 
• It is a mineral composed of **pure carbon.**
 
• Diamond is the smallest mass element capable of forming a stable covalently bonded crystal lattice with a highly symmetric and tightly bound structure.
 
• Diamond does not conduct electricity, is a **good electrical insulator.**
 
 
• Pure diamond is unable to conduct electricity because it lacks any delocalized free electrons in the carbon atom's outer shell.
 
 
 
• Diamond is a good **conductor of heat **due to its strong covalent bonding and low phonon scattering.
 
• All of the carbon atoms in the diamond lattice are **sp³ hybridized.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Graphite** is a crystalline form of carbon with its atoms arranged in a hexagonal structure.

 
 
• Graphite is a good conductor of electricity.
 
 
 
• **Gold** is a chemical element with the **atomic number 79**.
 
 
• Gold is a good conductor of both electricity and heat.
 
 
 
• **Soils** are electric current conductors.

questions.question: Mendel proposed the law of independent assortment on the basis of __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**dihybrid crosses**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Mendel proposed the law of independent assortment based on his experiments with **dihybrid crosses**.
 
• In his experiments, Mendel crossed plants that differed in two traits and observed the inheritance patterns of these traits in the offspring.
 
• The results led to the conclusion that the alleles of different genes assort independently

questions.question: The deficiency of Vitamin A causes:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**night blindness**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The deficiency of Vitamin A causes **night blindness**.
 
• **Vitamin A deficiency** can stem from insufficient dietary intake, issues with fat absorption, or liver-related disorders.
 
• This deficiency can compromise immune function and the production of blood cells, leading to symptoms such as skin rashes and characteristic eye problems like xerophthalmia and night blindness.
 
• Diagnosis often relies on identifying these ocular manifestations alongside low levels of vitamin A in the body.
 
• Treatment typically involves oral supplementation of vitamin A, although in severe cases or when malabsorption is a factor, administration via injection may be necessary.
 
• Foods rich in preformed vitamin A include fish liver oils, liver, egg yolks, butter, and dairy products fortified with vitamin A.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Beriberi **is a condition resulting from a deficiency of thiamine, also known as vitamin B1. The term "beriberi" originates from a Sinhalese word meaning "extreme weakness".
 
• **Scurvy** is a disorder caused by a significant deficiency of vitamin C in the diet. It is characterized by severe symptoms of vitamin C deficiency.
 
• **Rickets** is a condition characterized by the softening and weakening of bones in children, typically due to prolonged and severe deficiency of vitamin D.

questions.question: Identify a carbohydrate but does not fit into the definition.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the__** Rhamnose**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• While all the listed options are carbohydrates, **rhamnose doesn't strictly adhere to the classic definition of a carbohydrate.**
 
• The** general formula for carbohydrates is (CH2O)n, where n is an integer.**
 
• Rhamnose, however, has a slightly different formula: C6H12O5.
 
• **Rhamnose** is often categorized as a non-standard sugar because it has a different structural configuration.
 
• Rhamnose is important in plant biology and can be involved in the structure of certain polysaccharides, such as rhamnogalacturonan, which is found in pectin.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sucrose**:

 
 
• A disaccharide composed of glucose and fructose.
 
• Sucrose is commonly known as table sugar and is naturally found in many plants, particularly in sugarcane and sugar beets. 
 
 
 
• **Fructose**:
 
 
• A monosaccharide (simple sugar). 
 
• Fructose is often referred to as "fruit sugar" because it is found in many fruits and honey, and it is sweeter than glucose.
 
 
 
• **Maltose**:
 
 
• A disaccharide composed of two glucose units.
 
• Maltose is commonly found in malted foods and beverages, such as malted milk and beer, and is produced during the fermentation process.

questions.question: Which one of the following is a rare disease caused by the deficiency of Vitamin D that causes the bones to become soft and to bend?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Rickets.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rickets is a childhood disorder of the bones where the bones become soft and prone to fractures. Bones tend to become weak due to an inadequate supply of nutrients, Vitamin D3 in particular.**
 
• It is also caused due to a** lack of calcium and phosphate** in the body. Weak bones can lead to bone deformities. Vitamin D largely comes from exposing the skin to sunlight.
 
• Other good sources of Vitamin D are fatty fish (such as tuna and salmon) and egg yolks.
 
• **Rickets** is a disease associated with the deficiency of **Vitamin D**.
 
• Rickets is of the following types:
 
 
• **Nutritional Rickets** -
 
 
• This is caused due to intake of food which lacks calcium, phosphorous, and vitamin D.
 
 
 
• **Hypophosphatemic Rickets-**
 
 
• It is caused due to low levels of phosphate. It is an X-linked genetic disorder where the kidneys are not able to control the amount of phosphate excreted in the urine.
 
 
 
• **Renal Rickets-**
 
 
• People suffering from kidney disorders have renal rickets. They are unable to regulate the amount of calcium and phosphate excreted in the urine.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pernicious Anemia:**

 
 
• It is a decrease in red blood cells that occurs when the intestines cannot properly absorb vitamin B1.
 
• Vitamin B12 is also referred to as cobalamin because it contains a metal ion. Cyanocobalamin is used in vitamin supplements and pharmaceuticals.
 
• Symptoms of Vitamin B12 deficiency are the smoothness of the tongue, gastrointestinal disturbances, nervous symptoms.
 
 
 
• **Lupus:**
 
 
• It is caused by the lack of immunity in the body.

questions.question: Anant's mother advised him to not sleep under the trees at night as trees release ______ at night.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**release of carbon dioxide.**__

__
 
• The **carbon dioxide** that is produced during **human respiration** reaches the empty spaces within the leaves and simultaneously photosynthesis is going on.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• Due to this, **carbon dioxide **present in the air is used and **consumed by the plants**.
 
• Thus during the day, plants produce oxygen while **consuming carbon dioxide but at the night the process of photosynthesis stops but respiration continues for plants.**
 
 
• Meaning that **oxygen is not produced by the plants at night.**
 
 
 
• Because of this **natural phenomenon, **it is advised that at night if you sleep under the tree, you will not get oxygen, which can cause **breathing problems, suffocation, etc.**
